To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the proposed RACOG and the wRACOG approaches can be used to generate minority class samples that have high probability of being mis-classified by an existing learning model, (b) RACOG and WACOG can significantly improve the classification performance of learning models when applied to data with inherent class imbalance, and (c) RACOG can significantly reduce the computational time required for generating minority class samples.
the proposed RACOG and the wRACOG methods outperform existing resampling techniques in terms of accuracy, F-measure, and area under the ROC curve.
RACOG and its weighted version wRACOG are two novel oversampling techniques for addressing the class imbalance problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new probabilistic oversampling technique to address the class imbalance problem.
the development of a novel approach for addressing the class imbalance problem and its application in a complex real world problem domain.
developing new techniques for generating new samples from an under-represented class and using these samples to improve the classification accuracy of learning models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RACOG and/or wRACOG are the most suitable oversampling techniques for addressing the class imbalance problem.
the proposed approaches, namely RACEG and wRACO, outperformed all the existing resampling techniques.
RACOG and especially wRACOG outperforms the other resampling techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methods significantly outperformed the other methods in all the experiments.
the proposed approaches outperform other existing oversampling techniques in terms of classification performance.
the proposed approaches outperform existing techniques in most cases and are able to handle class imbalanced data sets with extreme class imbalance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wRACOG outperforms RACOG and other resampling techniques in terms of classification accuracy, F-score, and area under the ROC curve (AUC).
the proposed methods can be used to generate synthetic data samples that are more representative of the minority class.
the two proposed approaches can significantly improve the performance of the existing learning model on imbalanced data sets, while the existing approaches are not as effective.
